dimensions.assessment: Involves the Department of Justice and 35 named federal agencies compiling regulatory data, which will ultimately be published for public access.
dimensions.evidence: the head of each Federal agency described ... shall submit to the Committee on the Judiciary ... a report

dimensions.assessment: Requires extensive administrative data compilation and creation of public indexes covering 15 years of past prosecutions and violations.
dimensions.evidence: establish a publically accessible index of each criminal statutory offense

dimensions.assessment: The bill explicitly states that nothing in the section shall be construed to require or authorize appropriations.
dimensions.evidence: Nothing in this section shall be construed to require or authorize appropriations.

dimensions.assessment: Imposes reporting and database-creation duties across nearly all major federal departments and independent regulatory commissions.
dimensions.evidence: The Federal agencies described in this paragraph are the Department of Agriculture, the Department of Commerce...

dimensions.assessment: Requires initial reports within 1 year and public indexes within 2 years, establishing permanent public databases.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act ... establish a publically accessible index

missing_information: The exact number of criminal statutory and regulatory offenses that exist is unknown until the reports are completed.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill mandates comprehensive reports and public databases from the Department of Justice and dozens of federal agencies cataloging all criminal statutory and regulatory offenses, explicitly barring new appropriations.
